Day 3 | Partnerships, Fundraising Readiness & Founder Evolution

The final day of DERBI Foundation’s Acceleration Program focused on building long-term scale engines - partnerships, investor readiness, and leadership evolution.

We began with “Channel & Partnerships: Designing a Partner Engine That Scales,” led by Venkat Shyam. Founders explored how structured channel #strategies, aligned incentives, and ecosystem #collaborations can unlock non-linear growth beyond direct sales.

In the #Fundraising Deep Dive: #Investor-Grade Company — From Pitch to Process & Metrics That Raise Money, Ravindra Krishnappa emphasized building companies that are investment-ready by design. The session broke down traction KPIs, investors' trust, #governance discipline, narrative clarity, and process maturity.

The program concluded with “Org & Leadership for Scaling: Founder-to-CEO Transition” led by Sathyanarayana B V, followed by final reflections and key takeaways. The conversation centered on building leadership depth, creating accountable org structures, and evolving from operator to strategic decision-maker. Sathyanarayana B V also spoke about #HR Management Grid, Leadership styles, how each one of them affects and has an impact in different workplaces, and how leaders are born or lost under different #leadership style

Scaling a startup ultimately requires more than #strategy - it demands founder transformation.

We thank all our expert #mentors and participating #founders for making this acceleration journey deeply insightful and impact-driven. At DERBI Foundation, our commitment remains clear: enabling startups with the right #ecosystem, right #frameworks, and right #mentorship to scale sustainably.

Day 2 | Expanding Markets, Strengthening Financial Foundations

Day 2 of DERBI Foundation’s Acceleration Program shifted the lens from internal readiness to external expansion and financial resilience.

The day opened with “Market Access Strategy: #IndiaExpansion + Global Entry Readiness” led by Shivi Jain. Startups explored structured approaches to entering new markets, from regulatory preparedness and localization strategy to channel partnerships and #global positioning. The focus was on building scalable access, not opportunistic expansion.

In the Cashflow & Working Capital War-Room: Scale Without Dying, Nayak guided founders through one of the most underestimated growth levers — liquidity discipline. Through real-world scenarios and financial stress-testing frameworks, startups examined burn cycles, receivables management, and #capital efficiency as core survival metrics.

The day concluded with “Deal Structuring & Term Sheet Masterclass: Don’t Lose the Company” by Sharath Shyamasunder, The Startup Zone, where founders unpacked #investor clauses, dilution mechanics, control rights, and long-term implications of #fundraising decisions.

Growth is exciting. But #sustainable scale is built on informed expansion, disciplined capital management, and smart deal-making.

Over ten years, Social Alpha has backed more than 450 Indian start-ups solving problems conventional capital would not touch: a cryogen-free MRI machine, biodigesters running in more than 100,000 households, incense sticks made from temple flowers pulled from the Ganges. Those companies have gone on to raise more than $150 million in follow-on capital.

Social Alpha's wager is that markets can be built. De-risk the venture, align state, society, and capital, and a risk mainstream investors once refused becomes one they can underwrite.

I spent the past several months writing the Stanford University Graduate School of Business GSB case on Social Alpha with Professor William Barnett. What Manoj, Vidya Phalke, and the full team at Social Alpha have built deserves to be studied, and replicated well beyond India.
